source.text: Μετὰ ταῦτα εἶδον ἄλλον ἄγγελον καταβαίνοντα ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, ἔχοντα ἐξουσίαν μεγάλην, καὶ ἡ γῆ ἐφωτίσθη ἐκ τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: After these things I saw another angel coming down out of the heaven, having authority great, and the earth was lit up from the glory of him.

en.L: After these things I saw another angel coming down from heaven, having great authority, and the earth was lit up by his glory.
en.B: After this I saw another angel coming down from heaven. He had great authority, and the earth shone with his glory.
en.R: Then I saw another angel coming down from heaven. He had great power. His glory was so bright that it lit up the whole earth.

fr.L: Après ces choses, je vis un autre ange descendre du ciel, ayant une grande autorité, et la terre fut illuminée par sa gloire.
fr.B: Après cela, je vis un autre ange qui descendait du ciel. Il avait une grande autorité, et la terre resplendit de sa gloire.
fr.R: Puis j’ai vu un autre ange descendre du ciel. Il avait un grand pouvoir. Sa gloire était si brillante qu’elle a éclairé toute la terre.

sw.L: Baada ya mambo haya nilimwona malaika mwingine akishuka kutoka mbinguni, mwenye mamlaka makuu, na dunia ikaangazwa kwa utukufu wake.
sw.B: Baada ya hayo nilimwona malaika mwingine akishuka kutoka mbinguni. Alikuwa na mamlaka makuu, na dunia ikang'aa kwa utukufu wake.
sw.R: Kisha nikamwona malaika mwingine akishuka kutoka mbinguni. Alikuwa na uwezo mkubwa. Utukufu wake ulikuwa na mwanga mwingi hata ukaimulika dunia yote.

es.L: Después de estas cosas vi a otro ángel que descendía del cielo, que tenía gran autoridad, y la tierra fue iluminada por su gloria.
es.B: Después de esto vi a otro ángel que bajaba del cielo. Tenía gran autoridad, y la tierra se iluminó con su gloria.
es.R: Luego vi a otro ángel que bajaba del cielo. Tenía mucho poder. Su gloria era tan brillante que iluminó toda la tierra.

decisions.choice: the earth lit by his glory: Ezekiel 43:2
decisions.reason: When God's glory returned to the temple, "the earth shone with his glory" (Ezekiel 43:2). The angel comes from God's presence and reflects his brightness.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R) ("je vis" / "j’ai vu"); the heavenly voices and the laments keep their own tenses
decisions.reason: As in chapters 12 and 17: John tells what he saw, so the passé simple serves careful written narrative and Readable uses the passé composé. The chapter is mostly speech (the angels, the voice from heaven, the kings, merchants and sailors), which uses the present, the future and the passé composé at every level. This holds for the whole chapter.

source.text: καὶ ἔκραξεν ἐν ἰσχυρᾷ φωνῇ λέγων· Ἔπεσεν, ἔπεσεν Βαβυλὼν ἡ μεγάλη, καὶ ἐγένετο κατοικητήριον δαιμονίων καὶ φυλακὴ παντὸς πνεύματος ἀκαθάρτου καὶ φυλακὴ παντὸς ὀρνέου ἀκαθάρτου καὶ φυλακὴ παντὸς θηρίου ἀκαθάρτου καὶ μεμισημένου, ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ οἴνου τοῦ θυμοῦ τῆς πορνείας αὐτῆς πέπτωκαν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, καὶ οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς μετ’ αὐτῆς ἐπόρνευσαν, καὶ οἱ ἔμποροι τῆς γῆς ἐκ τῆς δυνάμεως τοῦ στρήνους αὐτῆς ἐπλούτησαν.

records.literal_gloss: And he cried out in mighty voice saying: Fell, fell Babylon the great, and became a dwelling of demons and a prison of every spirit unclean and a prison of every bird unclean and a prison of every beast unclean and having been hated, \v 3 because of the wine of the passion of the immorality of her have fallen all the nations, and the kings of the earth with her committed immorality, and the merchants of the earth from the power of the luxury of her became rich.

en.L: And he cried out with a mighty voice, saying, "Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great! She has become a dwelling place of demons and a haunt of every unclean spirit and a haunt of every unclean bird and a haunt of every unclean and hated beast, \v 3 for all the nations have fallen by the wine of the passion of her sexual immorality, and the kings of the earth committed sexual immorality with her, and the merchants of the earth grew rich from the power of her luxury."
en.B: He shouted with a mighty voice: "Babylon the great has fallen, has fallen! She has become a home for demons, a lair for every unclean spirit, a lair for every unclean bird, a lair for every unclean and hateful beast. \v 3 Through the wine of her raging immorality all the nations have fallen; the kings of the earth committed immorality with her, and the earth's merchants grew rich from her extravagant luxury."
en.R: He shouted with a powerful voice, "Babylon the great city has fallen! It has fallen! Now it is a home for demons and for every kind of evil spirit. It is a place where unclean birds and hated animals live. \v 3 All the nations fell because they drank the wine of her sexual sins. The kings of the earth committed sexual sins with her. The merchants of the earth became rich because she spent so much on luxuries."

fr.L: Et il cria d’une voix forte, disant : « Elle est tombée, elle est tombée, Babylone la grande ! Elle est devenue une demeure de démons, et un repaire de tout esprit impur, et un repaire de tout oiseau impur, et un repaire de toute bête impure et haïe, \v 3 car du vin de la passion de sa prostitution toutes les nations sont tombées, et les rois de la terre se sont prostitués avec elle, et les marchands de la terre se sont enrichis par la puissance de son luxe. »
fr.B: Il cria d’une voix puissante : « Elle est tombée, elle est tombée, Babylone la grande ! Elle est devenue la demeure des démons, le repaire de tout esprit impur, le repaire de tout oiseau impur, le repaire de toute bête impure et odieuse. \v 3 Par le vin de sa débauche effrénée, toutes les nations sont tombées ; les rois de la terre ont partagé sa débauche, et les marchands de la terre se sont enrichis de son luxe démesuré. »
fr.R: Il a crié d’une voix puissante : « Babylone, la grande ville, est tombée ! Elle est tombée ! Maintenant, c’est une maison pour les démons et pour toutes sortes d’esprits mauvais. C’est un endroit où vivent les oiseaux impurs et les animaux qu’on déteste. \v 3 Toutes les nations sont tombées, parce qu’elles ont bu le vin de son immoralité. Les rois de la terre ont eu des relations immorales avec elle. Les marchands de la terre sont devenus riches, parce qu’elle dépensait énormément pour son luxe. »

sw.L: Naye akapaza sauti kwa sauti yenye nguvu, akisema, "Ameanguka, ameanguka Babeli mkuu! Naye amekuwa makao ya mapepo, na ngome ya kila roho mchafu, na ngome ya kila ndege mchafu, na ngome ya kila mnyama mchafu na anayechukiwa, \v 3 kwa sababu mataifa yote yameanguka kwa divai ya tamaa kali ya uasherati wake, na wafalme wa dunia walizini naye, na wafanyabiashara wa dunia walitajirika kwa nguvu ya anasa zake."
sw.B: Akapiga kelele kwa sauti kuu: "Ameanguka, ameanguka Babeli mkuu! Amekuwa makao ya pepo, pango la kila roho mchafu, pango la kila ndege mchafu, pango la kila mnyama mchafu na wa kuchukiza. \v 3 Kwa divai ya uasherati wake uliokithiri mataifa yote yameanguka; wafalme wa dunia walizini naye, na wafanyabiashara wa dunia walitajirika kwa anasa zake zisizo na kiasi."
sw.R: Alipiga kelele kwa sauti yenye nguvu, "Babeli, ule mji mkuu, umeanguka! Umeanguka! Sasa ni makao ya pepo na ya kila aina ya roho waovu. Ni mahali wanapoishi ndege wachafu na wanyama wanaochukiwa. \v 3 Mataifa yote yalianguka kwa sababu yalikunywa divai ya dhambi zake za zinaa. Wafalme wa dunia walifanya dhambi za zinaa pamoja naye. Wafanyabiashara wa dunia walitajirika kwa sababu alitumia mali nyingi mno kwa anasa."

es.L: Y gritó con voz potente, diciendo: «¡Cayó, cayó Babilonia la grande! Y se ha convertido en morada de demonios y guarida de todo espíritu impuro y guarida de toda ave impura y guarida de toda bestia impura y aborrecida, \v 3 porque por el vino del furor de su inmoralidad sexual han caído todas las naciones, y los reyes de la tierra cometieron inmoralidad sexual con ella, y los comerciantes de la tierra se enriquecieron por el poder de su lujo».
es.B: Gritó con voz potente: «¡Ha caído, ha caído Babilonia la grande! Se ha convertido en casa de demonios, en guarida de todo espíritu impuro, en guarida de toda ave impura, en guarida de toda bestia impura y aborrecible. \v 3 Por el vino de su desenfrenada inmoralidad han caído todas las naciones; los reyes de la tierra cometieron inmoralidad con ella, y los comerciantes de la tierra se hicieron ricos con su lujo desmedido».
es.R: Gritó con voz fuerte: «¡Ha caído la gran ciudad de Babilonia! ¡Ha caído! Ahora es la casa de los demonios y de toda clase de espíritus malignos. Es un lugar donde viven aves impuras y animales odiados. \v 3 Todas las naciones cayeron porque bebieron el vino de sus pecados sexuales. Los reyes de la tierra cometieron pecados sexuales con ella. Los comerciantes de la tierra se hicieron ricos porque ella gastaba muchísimo en lujos».

decisions.choice: a ruin haunted by wild creatures: the prophets on Babylon and Edom
decisions.reason: The cry "Fallen, fallen is Babylon" is Isaiah's (21:9; compare 14:8). The prophets describe fallen Babylon and Edom as ruins where jackals, owls and wild goats live and demons haunt (Isaiah 13:19-22; 34:11-15; Jeremiah 50:39; 51:37). φυλακὴ means a prison or guarded place: the city becomes the haunt of everything unclean.

decisions.choice: have fallen
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads πέπτωκαν, "have fallen": the nations have fallen through the wine of her immorality. Many manuscripts have a word that differs by a letter and means "have drunk" (compare 14:8; 17:2). The translation follows the SBLGNT. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: luxury: extravagance and arrogance
decisions.reason: στρήνους means excessive luxury, with the insolence that goes with it. Her wealth made the merchants rich (18:11-19).

decisions.choice: haunt (L); lair (B); a place where ... live (R)
decisions.reason: The word means a guarded place; "haunt" and "lair" say what it is in a ruined city (m1).

decisions.choice: un repaire (L, B); le vin de la passion (L), sa débauche effrénée (B)
decisions.reason: "Repaire" is the French word for the hiding place of wild creatures and serves for both the English "haunt" and "lair" (r-en-1). For the wine, "fureur" would point to God's anger, which is not the sense here; Literal says "passion", and Balanced turns it into an adjective, as the English "raging" does.

decisions.choice: ngome (L); pango (B); mahali wanapoishi (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is a prison or a watch-post, here a place where such creatures stay (m1); Literal says "ngome" (stronghold), Balanced "pango" (lair), Readable "the place where they live", following the English haunt, lair and place.

decisions.choice: mapepo (L); pepo (B, R); roho mchafu (L, B), roho waovu (R)
decisions.reason: Demons are "pepo" (Literal uses the plural "mapepo" to keep them apart from the spirits that follow), and the unclean spirits "roho wachafu", "roho waovu" at Readable, as in 16:13.

decisions.choice: han caído
decisions.reason: Spanish follows the text the English follows, as the footnoted meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: comerciantes
decisions.reason: "Comerciante" is the ordinary modern word for a merchant; it is used for the whole chapter.

source.text: Καὶ ἤκουσα ἄλλην φωνὴν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ λέγουσαν· Ἐξέλθατε, ὁ λαός μου, ἐξ αὐτῆς, ἵνα μὴ συγκοινωνήσητε ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις αὐτῆς, καὶ ἐκ τῶν πληγῶν αὐτῆς ἵνα μὴ λάβητε·

records.literal_gloss: And I heard another voice out of the heaven saying: Come out, the people of me, out of her, so that not you share in the sins of her, and out of the plagues of her that not you receive,

en.L: And I heard another voice from heaven saying, "Come out of her, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, so that you do not share in her sins, and so that you do not receive any of her plagues,
en.B: Then I heard another voice from heaven: "Leave her, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, so that you have no part in her sins and do not suffer any of her plagues.
en.R: Then I heard another voice from heaven. It said, "My people, come out of that city! Then you will not join in her sins, and you will not suffer from her plagues.

fr.L: Et j’entendis une autre voix [venant] du ciel, qui disait : « Sortez d’elle, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple, afin de ne pas avoir part à ses péchés, et afin de ne rien recevoir de ses fléaux,
fr.B: Puis j’entendis une autre voix venant du ciel : « Quittez-la, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple, pour ne pas avoir part à ses péchés et ne pas subir ses fléaux.
fr.R: Puis j’ai entendu une autre voix venant du ciel. Elle disait : « Mon peuple, sortez de cette ville ! Alors vous ne participerez pas à ses péchés, et vous ne souffrirez pas de ses fléaux.

sw.L: Nami nikasikia sauti nyingine kutoka mbinguni ikisema, "Tokeni kwake, enyi watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, ili msishiriki dhambi zake, na ili msipokee [chochote] katika mapigo yake,
sw.B: Kisha nikasikia sauti nyingine kutoka mbinguni: "Enyi watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, tokeni kwake, ili msishiriki dhambi zake, wala msipatwe na mapigo yake yoyote.
sw.R: Kisha nikasikia sauti nyingine kutoka mbinguni. Ilisema, "Watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, tokeni katika mji huo! Hapo hamtashiriki dhambi zake, wala hamtateseka kwa mapigo yake.

es.L: Y oí otra voz del cielo que decía: «{{plural_you:Salgan|Salid}} de ella, pueblo {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}}, para que no {{plural_you:participen|participéis}} de sus pecados y para que no {{plural_you:reciban|recibáis}} de sus plagas,
es.B: Entonces oí otra voz del cielo: «{{plural_you:Salgan|Salid}} de ella, pueblo {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}}, para que no {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} parte en sus pecados ni {{plural_you:sufran|sufráis}} ninguna de sus plagas.
es.R: Luego oí otra voz del cielo. Decía: «¡Pueblo {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}}, {{plural_you:salgan|salid}} de esa ciudad! Así no {{plural_you:participarán|participaréis}} en sus pecados, y no {{plural_you:sufrirán|sufriréis}} sus plagas.

decisions.choice: Come out of her, my people: the call to leave Babylon
decisions.reason: The prophets called God's people to flee Babylon before its fall (Jeremiah 50:8; 51:6, 45; Isaiah 48:20; 52:11), and Paul applies the words to believers' separation from idolatry (2 Corinthians 6:17). The call is less about moving house than about refusing to share in the city's sins.

decisions.choice: my people: the speaker is God or Christ
decisions.reason: The voice speaks of "my people", so it is God's or Christ's. It continues to the end of 18:8.

decisions.choice: my: deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: The speaker is God or Christ (m2).

decisions.choice: pueblo {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}}
decisions.reason: The meaning decision says the speaker is God or Christ, so the possessive takes the deity pronoun span; Spanish places it after the noun, as in a call, where the span stays on the stressed form.

source.text: ὅτι ἐκολλήθησαν αὐτῆς αἱ ἁμαρτίαι ἄχρι τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ ἐμνημόνευσεν ὁ θεὸς τὰ ἀδικήματα αὐτῆς.

records.literal_gloss: because were heaped up of her the sins as far as the heaven, and remembered the God the crimes of her.

en.L: for her sins have piled up as far as heaven, and God has remembered her crimes.
en.B: For her sins have stacked up as high as heaven, and God has not forgotten her crimes.
en.R: Her sins are piled up as high as the sky. God remembers all the wrong things she has done.

fr.L: car ses péchés se sont amoncelés jusqu’au ciel, et Dieu s’est souvenu de ses crimes.
fr.B: Car ses péchés se sont entassés jusqu’au ciel, et Dieu n’a pas oublié ses crimes.
fr.R: Ses péchés sont empilés jusqu’au ciel. Dieu se souvient de tout le mal qu’elle a fait.

sw.L: kwa sababu dhambi zake zimerundikana mpaka mbinguni, na Mungu amekumbuka makosa yake.
sw.B: Kwa maana dhambi zake zimerundikana hadi mbinguni, na Mungu hajasahau maovu yake.
sw.R: Dhambi zake zimerundikana juu mpaka angani. Mungu anakumbuka mabaya yote aliyoyatenda.

es.L: porque sus pecados se han amontonado hasta el cielo, y Dios se ha acordado de sus maldades.
es.B: Porque sus pecados se han amontonado hasta el cielo, y Dios no ha olvidado sus crímenes.
es.R: Sus pecados se han amontonado tan alto que llegan hasta el cielo. Dios se acuerda de todo el mal que ella ha hecho.

decisions.choice: sins piled to heaven: Jeremiah 51:9
decisions.reason: "Her judgment has reached up to heaven" (Jeremiah 51:9; compare Genesis 18:20-21, the outcry against Sodom). ἐκολλήθησαν means stuck together, heaped up. God remembers in order to judge (16:19).

source.text: ἀπόδοτε αὐτῇ ὡς καὶ αὐτὴ ἀπέδωκεν, καὶ διπλώσατε τὰ διπλᾶ κατὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτῆς· ἐν τῷ ποτηρίῳ ᾧ ἐκέρασεν κεράσατε αὐτῇ διπλοῦν·

records.literal_gloss: Give back to her as also she gave back, and double the double according to the works of her; in the cup in which she mixed, mix for her double.

en.L: Pay her back as she herself paid back, and repay [her] double according to her works; in the cup that she mixed, mix double for her.
en.B: Treat her as she treated others; repay her twice over for her deeds; mix her a double draught in the very cup she mixed.
en.R: Do to her what she did to others. Pay her back twice as much for what she has done. She mixed a drink of suffering for others. Now mix her a drink twice as strong.

fr.L: Rendez-lui comme elle-même a rendu, et rendez-[lui] le double selon ses œuvres ; dans la coupe où elle a mélangé, mélangez-lui le double.
fr.B: Traitez-la comme elle a traité les autres ; rendez-lui le double de ce qu’elle a fait ; dans la coupe même où elle a préparé son breuvage, préparez-lui-en un deux fois plus fort.
fr.R: Faites-lui ce qu’elle a fait aux autres. Rendez-lui deux fois plus que ce qu’elle a fait. Elle a préparé pour les autres une boisson de souffrance. Maintenant, préparez-lui une boisson deux fois plus forte.

sw.L: Mlipeni kama yeye mwenyewe alivyolipa, na mzidishieni mara mbili kulingana na matendo yake; katika kikombe alichochanganya, mchanganyieni mara mbili.
sw.B: Mtendeeni kama yeye alivyowatendea wengine; mlipeni mara mbili kwa matendo yake; katika kikombe kile kile alichochanganya, mchanganyieni kinywaji mara mbili zaidi.
sw.R: Mtendeeni yale aliyowatendea wengine. Mlipeni mara mbili kwa mabaya aliyoyatenda. Aliwachanganyia wengine kinywaji cha mateso. Sasa mchanganyieni kinywaji chenye nguvu mara mbili zaidi.

es.L: {{plural_you:Páguenle|Pagadle}} como ella también pagó, y {{plural_you:denle|dadle}} el doble conforme a sus obras; en la copa en que ella mezcló, {{plural_you:mézclenle|mezcladle}} el doble.
es.B: {{plural_you:Trátenla|Tratadla}} como ella trató a otros; {{plural_you:páguenle|pagadle}} el doble por lo que ha hecho; en la misma copa en que ella preparó bebida, {{plural_you:prepárenle|preparadle}} el doble.
es.R: {{plural_you:Háganle|Hacedle}} a ella lo que ella hizo a otros. {{plural_you:Páguenle|Pagadle}} el doble por lo que ha hecho. Ella preparó una bebida de sufrimiento para otros. Ahora {{plural_you:prepárenle|preparadle}} a ella una bebida dos veces más fuerte.

decisions.choice: double: full repayment
alternatives: literally twice the harm she did
decisions.reason: In the prophets "double" can mean a full and fitting measure (Jeremiah 16:18; Isaiah 40:2). The point is that her judgment matches her deeds completely, as 18:7 says: "as much as she glorified herself".

decisions.choice: addressed to the agents of judgment
decisions.reason: The commands are most likely addressed to those who carry out God's judgment, such as the angels or the beast and the ten horns (17:16). God's people are told to leave the city (18:4), not to take revenge (Romans 12:19).

decisions.choice: plural commands (plural_you)
decisions.reason: The commands are addressed to more than one, the agents of judgment, as the meaning decision says, so every verb is a plural_you span.

source.text: ὅσα ἐδόξασεν αὑτὴν καὶ ἐστρηνίασεν, τοσοῦτον δότε αὐτῇ βασανισμὸν καὶ πένθος.

records.literal_gloss: As much as she glorified herself and lived in luxury, so much give to her torment and grief.

en.L: As much as she glorified herself and lived in luxury, so much torment and grief give her.
en.B: In proportion to the glory she gave herself and the luxury she lived in, give her torment and mourning.
en.R: She gave herself glory and lived in luxury. Now give her the same amount of pain and sorrow.

fr.L: Autant elle s’est glorifiée et a vécu dans le luxe, autant donnez-lui de tourment et de deuil.
fr.B: À la mesure de la gloire qu’elle s’est donnée et du luxe où elle a vécu, donnez-lui tourment et deuil.
fr.R: Elle s’est donné de la gloire et elle a vécu dans le luxe. Maintenant, donnez-lui autant de douleur et de tristesse.

sw.L: Kwa kadiri alivyojitukuza na kuishi kwa anasa, kwa kadiri hiyo mpeni mateso na huzuni.
sw.B: Kwa kipimo cha utukufu aliojipa na anasa alizoishi nazo, mpeni mateso na maombolezo.
sw.R: Alijipa utukufu na kuishi kwa anasa. Sasa mpeni maumivu na huzuni kwa kiasi kile kile.

es.L: Cuanto se glorificó a sí misma y vivió en lujo, tanto tormento y llanto {{plural_you:denle|dadle}}.
es.B: En la medida en que se dio gloria a sí misma y vivió en el lujo, {{plural_you:denle|dadle}} tormento y llanto.
es.R: Ella se dio gloria a sí misma y vivió en el lujo. Ahora {{plural_you:denle|dadle}} la misma medida de dolor y tristeza.

decisions.choice: the measure of her pride is the measure of her judgment
decisions.reason: She claimed the glory that belongs to God (compare 14:7; 15:4). Her judgment matches her self-exaltation.

source.text: ὅτι ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτῆς λέγει ὅτι Κάθημαι βασίλισσα, καὶ χήρα οὐκ εἰμί, καὶ πένθος οὐ μὴ ἴδω.

records.literal_gloss: because in the heart of her she says: I sit a queen and a widow not I am, and grief not not I see.

en.L: For in her heart she says, 'I sit as a queen, and I am not a widow, and I will never see grief.'
en.B: In her heart she keeps saying, 'Here I sit, a queen; I am not a widow, and mourning I will never see.'
en.R: She says to herself, 'I am a queen sitting on my throne. I am not a widow. I will never be sad.'

fr.L: Car dans son cœur elle dit : “Je siège en reine, et je ne suis pas veuve, et je ne verrai jamais le deuil.”
fr.B: Dans son cœur, elle ne cesse de dire : “Je trône ici en reine ; je ne suis pas veuve, et le deuil, je ne le verrai jamais.”
fr.R: Elle se dit : “Je suis une reine assise sur mon trône. Je ne suis pas veuve. Je ne serai jamais triste.”

sw.L: Kwa sababu moyoni mwake anasema, 'Nimeketi malkia, wala mimi si mjane, wala sitaona huzuni kamwe.'
sw.B: Moyoni mwake anaendelea kusema, 'Hapa nimeketi, malkia; mimi si mjane, wala sitaona maombolezo kamwe.'
sw.R: Anajiambia, 'Mimi ni malkia, nimeketi juu ya kiti changu cha enzi. Mimi si mjane. Sitahuzunika kamwe.'

es.L: Porque en su corazón dice: “Estoy sentada como reina, y no soy viuda, y jamás veré llanto”.
es.B: En su corazón sigue diciendo: “Aquí estoy sentada, una reina; no soy viuda, y jamás conoceré el llanto”.
es.R: Ella se dice a sí misma: “Soy una reina sentada en mi trono. No soy viuda. Nunca estaré triste”.

decisions.choice: I sit as queen and am no widow: Isaiah 47
decisions.reason: Babylon said, "I shall be mistress forever ... I shall not sit as a widow or know the loss of children", and God replied that both would come on her in a moment, in one day (Isaiah 47:7-9; compare Zephaniah 2:15). John uses the same boast and the same answer (18:8).

decisions.choice: llanto
decisions.reason: The Greek word for mourning is rendered "llanto" throughout the chapter, so the threat in 18:7-8 and the merchants' weeping in 18:11, 15 and 19 echo one another.

es.B: Por eso, en un solo día le llegarán sus plagas: muerte, llanto y hambre, y el fuego la consumirá; porque poderoso es el Señor Dios que la ha juzgado».
es.R: Por eso en un solo día le pasarán cosas terribles: muerte, tristeza y hambre. Será quemada con fuego. El Señor Dios, que la juzga, es poderoso».

decisions.choice: in one day: the sudden fall of Isaiah 47:9
decisions.reason: See the note on 18:7. The judgment is sudden: in one day, and in one hour (18:10, 17, 19). The fire was foretold in 17:16.

source.text: Καὶ κλαύσουσιν καὶ κόψονται ἐπ’ αὐτὴν οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς οἱ μετ’ αὐτῆς πορνεύσαντες καὶ στρηνιάσαντες, ὅταν βλέπωσιν τὸν καπνὸν τῆς πυρώσεως αὐτῆς, ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἑστηκότες διὰ τὸν φόβον τοῦ βασανισμοῦ αὐτῆς λέγοντες· Οὐαὶ οὐαί, ἡ πόλις ἡ μεγάλη, Βαβυλὼν ἡ πόλις ἡ ἰσχυρά, ὅτι μιᾷ ὥρᾳ ἦλθεν ἡ κρίσις σου.

records.literal_gloss: And will weep and wail over her the kings of the earth, those with her having committed immorality and lived in luxury, when they see the smoke of the burning of her, \v 10 from afar standing because of the fear of the torment of her, saying: Woe woe, the city the great, Babylon the city the strong, because in one hour came the judgment of you.

en.L: And the kings of the earth who committed sexual immorality and lived in luxury with her will weep and wail over her when they see the smoke of her burning, \v 10 standing far off because of the fear of her torment, saying, "Woe, woe, the great city, Babylon, the strong city, for in one hour your judgment has come!"
en.B: The earth's kings, who shared her immorality and her luxury, will weep and beat their breasts over her as they watch the smoke rise from her burning. \v 10 Keeping far away for fear of her torment, they will say, "Woe, woe, great city, Babylon, city of strength! In a single hour your judgment has come."
en.R: The kings of the earth committed sexual sins with her and enjoyed her riches. When they see the smoke from her burning, they will cry and be very sad. \v 10 They will be afraid of her suffering, so they will stand far away. They will say, "How terrible! How terrible for you, great city, powerful city of Babylon! In just one hour your punishment has come!"

fr.L: Et ils pleureront et se lamenteront sur elle, les rois de la terre qui se sont prostitués et ont vécu dans le luxe avec elle, quand ils verront la fumée de son incendie, \v 10 se tenant au loin à cause de la crainte de son tourment, disant : « Malheur, malheur, ô grande ville, Babylone, ville forte, car en une heure ton jugement est venu ! »
fr.B: Les rois de la terre, qui ont partagé sa débauche et son luxe, pleureront sur elle et se frapperont la poitrine en voyant monter la fumée de son incendie. \v 10 Se tenant à distance par crainte de son tourment, ils diront : « Malheur, malheur à toi, grande ville, Babylone, ville puissante ! En une seule heure ton jugement est venu. »
fr.R: Les rois de la terre ont eu des relations immorales avec elle et ont profité de ses richesses. Quand ils verront la fumée de son incendie, ils pleureront et seront très tristes. \v 10 Ils auront peur de ses souffrances, alors ils resteront loin. Ils diront : « Quel malheur ! Quel malheur pour toi, grande ville, puissante ville de Babylone ! En une heure seulement, ta punition est arrivée ! »

sw.L: Na wafalme wa dunia waliozini pamoja naye na kuishi kwa anasa watalia na kuomboleza juu yake, watakapouona moshi wa kuungua kwake, \v 10 wakiwa wamesimama mbali kwa sababu ya kuogopa mateso yake, wakisema, "Ole, ole, mji ule mkubwa, Babeli, mji ule wenye nguvu, kwa sababu katika saa moja hukumu yako imekuja!"
sw.B: Wafalme wa dunia walioshiriki uasherati wake na anasa zake watamlilia na kujipiga vifua watakapouona moshi ukipanda kutoka katika kuungua kwake. \v 10 Watakaa mbali kwa kuogopa mateso yake, wakisema, "Ole, ole, mji mkuu, Babeli, mji wenye nguvu! Katika saa moja tu hukumu yako imekuja."
sw.R: Wafalme wa dunia walifanya dhambi za zinaa pamoja naye na kufurahia utajiri wake. Watakapoona moshi wa kuungua kwake, watalia na kuhuzunika sana. \v 10 Wataogopa mateso yake, kwa hiyo watasimama mbali. Watasema, "Ni msiba mkubwa! Msiba mkubwa umekupata, wewe mji mkuu, Babeli, mji wenye nguvu! Katika saa moja tu adhabu yako imekuja!"

es.L: Y llorarán y harán lamentación por ella los reyes de la tierra que cometieron inmoralidad sexual y vivieron en lujo con ella, cuando vean el humo de su incendio, \v 10 de pie a lo lejos por el temor de su tormento, diciendo: «¡Ay, ay, la gran ciudad, Babilonia, la ciudad poderosa, porque en una hora vino tu juicio!».
es.B: Los reyes de la tierra, que compartieron con ella su inmoralidad y su lujo, llorarán y se golpearán el pecho por ella al ver subir el humo de su incendio. \v 10 Manteniéndose lejos por miedo a su tormento, dirán: «¡Ay, ay de ti, gran ciudad, Babilonia, ciudad poderosa! ¡En una sola hora ha llegado tu juicio!».
es.R: Los reyes de la tierra cometieron pecados sexuales con ella y disfrutaron de sus riquezas. Cuando vean el humo del incendio, llorarán y estarán muy tristes. \v 10 Tendrán miedo de su sufrimiento, y por eso se quedarán lejos. Dirán: «¡Qué terrible! ¡Qué terrible para ti, gran ciudad, poderosa ciudad de Babilonia! ¡En solo una hora te ha llegado el castigo!».

decisions.choice: the laments over Tyre in Ezekiel 26-27
decisions.reason: The laments of kings, merchants and sailors follow Ezekiel's laments over Tyre, the great trading city, whose fall the princes of the coast, the merchants and the seamen mourned from a distance (Ezekiel 26:15-18; 27:28-36). Babylon's mourners grieve for their own losses more than for her.

decisions.choice: in one hour: suddenly
decisions.reason: The phrase is repeated in each lament (18:10, 17, 19): a city that seemed permanent is gone in a moment.

decisions.choice: Woe (L, B); How terrible (R)
decisions.reason: As in 8:13.

decisions.choice: Malheur, malheur (L, B); Quel malheur ! (R), here and in 18:16 and 18:19
decisions.reason: As the style guide's "Malheur à vous" for the whole New Testament. Here the cry is a lament over the city rather than a threat, which Readable makes plain with the exclamation "Quel malheur !", the everyday French for the English "How terrible!". Literal keeps the bare vocative with "ô", which French needs to address the city.

decisions.choice: ole (L, B); ni msiba mkubwa (R)
decisions.reason: "Ole" is the Swahili cry of woe, as settled for the Swahili New Testament; Readable says "ni msiba mkubwa" (what a disaster), as the English Readable says "How terrible". The same in 18:16 and 18:19.

decisions.choice: ¡Ay, ay! (L, B); ¡Qué terrible! (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for woe, as in 8:13, used for all three laments of the chapter.

decisions.choice: se golpearán el pecho
decisions.reason: The Greek verb is the gesture of mourning, beating the breast; Balanced names it, as the English does.

source.text: Καὶ οἱ ἔμποροι τῆς γῆς κλαίουσιν καὶ πενθοῦσιν ἐπ’ αὐτήν, ὅτι τὸν γόμον αὐτῶν οὐδεὶς ἀγοράζει οὐκέτι, γόμον χρυσοῦ καὶ ἀργύρου καὶ λίθου τιμίου καὶ μαργαριτῶν καὶ βυσσίνου καὶ πορφύρας καὶ σιρικοῦ καὶ κοκκίνου, καὶ πᾶν ξύλον θύϊνον καὶ πᾶν σκεῦος ἐλεφάντινον καὶ πᾶν σκεῦος ἐκ ξύλου τιμιωτάτου καὶ χαλκοῦ καὶ σιδήρου καὶ μαρμάρου, καὶ κιννάμωμον καὶ ἄμωμον καὶ θυμιάματα καὶ μύρον καὶ λίβανον καὶ οἶνον καὶ ἔλαιον καὶ σεμίδαλιν καὶ σῖτον καὶ κτήνη καὶ πρόβατα, καὶ ἵππων καὶ ῥεδῶν καὶ σωμάτων, καὶ ψυχὰς ἀνθρώπων.

records.literal_gloss: And the merchants of the earth weep and mourn over her, because the cargo of them no one buys any longer, \v 12 cargo of gold and of silver and of stone precious and of pearls and of fine linen and of purple and of silk and of scarlet, and all wood citron and every article of ivory and every article out of wood most precious and of bronze and of iron and of marble, \v 13 and cinnamon and spice and incenses and myrrh and frankincense and wine and oil and fine flour and wheat and cattle and sheep, and of horses and of carriages and of bodies, and souls of men.

en.L: And the merchants of the earth weep and mourn over her, because no one buys their cargo anymore, \v 12 cargo of gold and silver and precious stone and pearls and fine linen and purple and silk and scarlet, and all citron wood and every article of ivory and every article of most precious wood and bronze and iron and marble, \v 13 and cinnamon and spice and incense and myrrh and frankincense and wine and olive oil and fine flour and wheat and cattle and sheep, and of horses and of carriages, and of bodies, and souls of {{gender:human beings|men}}.
en.B: The merchants of the earth weep and mourn over her, because no one buys their goods any more: \v 12 goods of gold, silver, precious stones, and pearls; fine linen, purple, silk, and scarlet; all kinds of citron wood, and all sorts of objects of ivory, costly wood, bronze, iron, and marble; \v 13 cinnamon and spice, incense, myrrh, and frankincense; wine and olive oil, fine flour and wheat; cattle and sheep; horses and carriages; and slaves, human lives.
en.R: The merchants of the earth will cry and be sad about her, because no one buys their goods anymore. \v 12 They sold gold, silver, jewels, and pearls. They sold fine linen, purple cloth, silk, and red cloth. They sold sweet-smelling wood and things made of ivory, expensive wood, bronze, iron, and marble. \v 13 They sold cinnamon, spices, incense, myrrh, and frankincense. They sold wine, olive oil, flour, and wheat. They sold cattle, sheep, horses, and carriages. They even sold people as slaves.

fr.B: Les marchands de la terre pleurent et sont en deuil à cause d’elle, car personne n’achète plus leurs marchandises : \v 12 marchandises d’or, d’argent, de pierres précieuses et de perles ; de fin lin, de pourpre, de soie et d’écarlate ; toutes sortes de bois de thuya, toutes sortes d’objets d’ivoire, de bois précieux, de bronze, de fer et de marbre ; \v 13 cannelle et épices, parfums, myrrhe et encens ; vin et huile d’olive, fleur de farine et blé ; bœufs et moutons ; chevaux et chariots ; et des esclaves, des vies humaines.

Ils vendaient du lin fin, des tissus pourpres, de la soie et des tissus rouges. Ils vendaient du bois parfumé et des objets en ivoire, en bois précieux, en bronze, en fer et en marbre. \v 13 Ils vendaient de la cannelle, des épices, des parfums, de la myrrhe et de l’encens. Ils vendaient du vin, de l’huile d’olive, de la farine et du blé. Ils vendaient des bœufs, des moutons, des chevaux et des chariots. Ils vendaient même des gens comme esclaves.

sw.L: Na wafanyabiashara wa dunia wanalia na kuomboleza juu yake, kwa sababu hakuna mtu anayenunua tena shehena yao, \v 12 shehena ya dhahabu na fedha na kito cha thamani na lulu na kitani safi na zambarau na hariri na nguo nyekundu sana, na kila mti wa thuya na kila chombo cha pembe za ndovu na kila chombo cha mti wa thamani kuu na cha shaba na cha chuma na cha marumaru, \v 13 na mdalasini na viungo na uvumba na manemane na ubani na divai na mafuta ya zeituni na unga laini na ngano na ng'ombe na kondoo, na ya farasi na ya magari, na ya miili, na nafsi za wanadamu.

sw.R: Wafanyabiashara wa dunia watalia na kumhuzunikia, kwa sababu hakuna mtu anayenunua bidhaa zao tena. \v 12 Waliuza dhahabu, fedha, vito na lulu. Waliuza kitani safi, nguo za zambarau, hariri na nguo nyekundu. Waliuza mbao zenye harufu nzuri na vitu vilivyotengenezwa kwa pembe za ndovu, mbao za bei ghali, shaba, chuma na marumaru. \v 13 Waliuza mdalasini, viungo, uvumba, manemane na ubani. Waliuza divai, mafuta ya zeituni, unga na ngano. Waliuza ng'ombe, kondoo, farasi na magari ya farasi. Waliuza hata watu kuwa watumwa.

es.B: Los comerciantes de la tierra lloran y hacen duelo por ella, porque ya nadie compra sus mercancías: \v 12 mercancías de oro, plata, piedras preciosas y perlas; lino fino, púrpura, seda y escarlata; toda clase de madera de cidro, y toda clase de objetos de marfil, de maderas costosas, de bronce, de hierro y de mármol; \v 13 canela y especias, incienso, mirra y olíbano; vino y aceite de oliva, flor de harina y trigo; ganado y ovejas; caballos y carruajes; y esclavos, vidas humanas.
es.R: Los comerciantes de la tierra llorarán y estarán tristes por ella, porque ya nadie compra sus mercancías. \v 12 Vendían oro, plata, joyas y perlas. Vendían lino fino, telas de púrpura, seda y telas rojas. Vendían madera perfumada y objetos de marfil, de madera cara, de bronce, de hierro y de mármol. \v 13 Vendían canela, especias, incienso, mirra y olíbano. Vendían vino, aceite de oliva, harina y trigo. Vendían ganado, ovejas, caballos y carruajes. Hasta vendían personas como esclavos.

decisions.choice: the cargo list: Ezekiel 27
decisions.reason: Ezekiel 27:12-24 lists the goods that Tyre traded with every nation, ending with slaves (27:13). Here the list of luxuries that flowed into the great city ends the same way.

decisions.choice: citron wood: a costly, scented wood
decisions.reason: Citron wood from North Africa was prized in Rome for its grain and scent, and tables made from it were famously expensive.

decisions.choice: bodies, and souls of human beings: the slave trade
decisions.reason: σωμάτων, "bodies", was a common term for slaves in the market. "Souls of human beings" may explain it or add to it: what the city bought and sold included people's very lives. The list ends with its worst item.

decisions.choice: bodies, and souls of human beings (L); slaves, human lives (B); people as slaves (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek words; Balanced and Readable say what they meant (m3). "Slaves" stays at every level, as the style guide keeps it for people bought and sold.

decisions.choice: bois de thuya (L, B), bois parfumé (R); amome (L), épices (B, R)
decisions.reason: The costly scented wood (m2) is the North African thuya, and French has kept the name; "citronnier" would wrongly suggest the lemon tree. Literal names the spice "amome", a word French still has; Balanced and Readable say "épices", as the English does.

decisions.choice: mti wa thuya (L, B); mbao zenye harufu nzuri (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek names the scented wood of the thuya tree of North Africa (m2), not the fruit tree now called citron, so Swahili keeps the tree's name "thuya" and Balanced adds that the wood is fragrant; Readable says only "scented wood", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: miili, na nafsi za wanadamu (L); watumwa, yaani maisha ya wanadamu (B); watu kuwa watumwa (R)
decisions.reason: The last item is the slave trade (m3): Literal keeps the Greek "bodies, and souls of human beings"; Balanced names slaves and adds "maisha ya wanadamu" (human lives); Readable says they sold people as slaves. "Mtumwa" is kept at every level because slavery itself is the point. "Wanadamu" already covers men and women, so the English gender span has no counterpart.

decisions.choice: cuerpos, y almas de {{gender:seres humanos|hombres}} (L); esclavos, vidas humanas (B); personas como esclavos (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision says this is the slave trade; Literal keeps the Greek words, and Balanced and Readable say plainly what was sold.

decisions.choice: olíbano
decisions.reason: Two words for incense stand side by side; "incienso" renders the general word, and "olíbano" the resin called frankincense, so both stay distinct.

source.text: καὶ ἡ ὀπώρα σου τῆς ἐπιθυμίας τῆς ψυχῆς ἀπῆλθεν ἀπὸ σοῦ, καὶ πάντα τὰ λιπαρὰ καὶ τὰ λαμπρὰ ἀπώλετο ἀπὸ σοῦ, καὶ οὐκέτι οὐ μὴ αὐτὰ εὑρήσουσιν.

records.literal_gloss: And the ripe fruit of you of the desire of the soul went away from you, and all the rich things and the splendid things perished from you, and no longer not not them they will find.

en.L: And the ripe fruit of your soul's desire has gone from you, and all the rich and splendid things have perished from you, and never again will they find them.
en.B: The harvest of all that your heart desired has left you, and everything rich and dazzling is lost to you; no one will ever find it again.
en.R: Babylon, the good things you wanted so much are gone. All your riches and beautiful things have disappeared. No one will ever find them again.

fr.L: Et le fruit mûr du désir de ton âme s’en est allé loin de toi, et toutes les choses somptueuses et éclatantes sont perdues pour toi, et on ne les trouvera plus jamais.
fr.B: La récolte de tout ce que ton cœur désirait t’a quittée, et tout ce qui était somptueux et éblouissant est perdu pour toi ; on ne le retrouvera jamais plus.
fr.R: Babylone, les bonnes choses que tu désirais tant sont parties. Toutes tes richesses et tes belles choses ont disparu. Personne ne les retrouvera jamais.

sw.L: Na matunda yako uliyoyatamani kwa nafsi yako yamekuondokea, na vitu vyote vinono na vyenye kung'aa vimepotea kwako, wala hawatavipata tena kamwe.
sw.B: Mavuno ya yote ambayo moyo wako uliyatamani yamekuondokea, na kila kitu cha fahari na cha kung'aa kimepotea kwako; hakuna mtu atakayekipata tena kamwe.
sw.R: Babeli, vitu vizuri ulivyovitamani sana vimekwisha. Utajiri wako wote na vitu vyako vizuri vimetoweka. Hakuna mtu atakayevipata tena kamwe.

es.L: Y el fruto maduro del deseo de tu alma se ha apartado de ti, y todas las cosas exquisitas y espléndidas se te han perdido, y nunca más las hallarán.
es.B: La cosecha de todo lo que tu corazón deseaba se ha ido de ti, y todo lo exquisito y deslumbrante se te ha perdido; nunca más nadie lo volverá a encontrar.
es.R: Babilonia, las cosas buenas que tanto querías ya no están. Todas tus riquezas y tus cosas hermosas han desaparecido. Nadie las volverá a encontrar jamás.

decisions.choice: a sudden address to the city
decisions.reason: The account turns and speaks to the city directly, as in 18:22-23. "They will find" is impersonal: no one will find them.

decisions.choice: Babylon (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names the city being addressed.

decisions.choice: tú (the city addressed in the singular)
decisions.reason: The verse turns to speak to the city herself, so Spanish uses "tú", as in the laments of 18:10, 16 and 19.

source.text: οἱ ἔμποροι τούτων, οἱ πλουτήσαντες ἀπ’ αὐτῆς, ἀπὸ μακρόθεν στήσονται διὰ τὸν φόβον τοῦ βασανισμοῦ αὐτῆς κλαίοντες καὶ πενθοῦντες, λέγοντες· Οὐαὶ οὐαί, ἡ πόλις ἡ μεγάλη, ἡ περιβεβλημένη βύσσινον καὶ πορφυροῦν καὶ κόκκινον καὶ κεχρυσωμένη χρυσίῳ καὶ λίθῳ τιμίῳ καὶ μαργαρίτῃ, ὅτι μιᾷ ὥρᾳ ἠρημώθη ὁ τοσοῦτος πλοῦτος.

records.literal_gloss: The merchants of these things, the [ones] having become rich from her, from afar will stand because of the fear of the torment of her, weeping and mourning, \v 16 saying: Woe woe, the city the great, the [one] having been clothed in fine linen and purple and scarlet, and having been gilded with gold and stone precious and pearl, \v 17 because in one hour was laid waste the so great wealth.

en.L: The merchants of these things, who grew rich from her, will stand far off because of the fear of her torment, weeping and mourning, \v 16 saying, "Woe, woe, the great city, clothed in fine linen and purple and scarlet, and adorned with gold and precious stone and pearl, \v 17 for in one hour such great wealth has been laid waste!"
en.B: Those who dealt in these things and were made rich by her will keep their distance in fear of her torment, weeping and grieving: \v 16 "Woe, woe for the great city, which wore fine linen, purple, and scarlet, and was decked with gold, jewels, and pearls! \v 17 So much wealth, and in one hour it is ruined!"
en.R: The merchants who became rich by selling these things to her will stand far away. They will be afraid of her suffering. They will cry and be sad. \v 16 They will say, "How terrible! How terrible for the great city! She dressed in fine linen, purple, and red clothes. She wore gold, jewels, and pearls. \v 17 In just one hour all her riches are gone!"

fr.L: Les marchands de ces choses, qui se sont enrichis par elle, se tiendront au loin à cause de la crainte de son tourment, pleurant et en deuil, \v 16 disant : « Malheur, malheur, ô grande ville, vêtue de fin lin, de pourpre et d’écarlate, et parée d’or, de pierre précieuse et de perle, \v 17 car en une heure une si grande richesse a été dévastée ! »
fr.B: Ceux qui faisaient commerce de ces choses et qu’elle avait enrichis se tiendront à distance, par crainte de son tourment ; ils pleureront et seront en deuil : \v 16 « Malheur, malheur à la grande ville, qui était vêtue de fin lin, de pourpre et d’écarlate, et parée d’or, de pierres précieuses et de perles ! \v 17 Tant de richesses, et en une heure tout est ruiné ! »
fr.R: Les marchands qui sont devenus riches en lui vendant ces choses resteront loin. Ils auront peur de ses souffrances. Ils pleureront et seront tristes. \v 16 Ils diront : « Quel malheur ! Quel malheur pour la grande ville ! Elle s’habillait de lin fin, de pourpre et de rouge. Elle portait de l’or, des pierres précieuses et des perles. \v 17 En une heure seulement, toutes ses richesses ont disparu ! »

sw.L: Wafanyabiashara wa vitu hivi, waliotajirika kutoka kwake, watasimama mbali kwa sababu ya kuogopa mateso yake, wakilia na kuomboleza, \v 16 wakisema, "Ole, ole, mji ule mkubwa, uliovikwa kitani safi na zambarau na nyekundu sana, na kupambwa kwa dhahabu na kito cha thamani na lulu, \v 17 kwa sababu katika saa moja utajiri mwingi namna hii umeharibiwa!"
sw.B: Wale waliofanya biashara ya vitu hivyo na kutajirishwa naye watakaa mbali kwa kuogopa mateso yake, wakilia na kuomboleza: \v 16 "Ole, ole, mji mkuu, uliovaa kitani safi, zambarau na nyekundu sana, na kupambwa kwa dhahabu, vito na lulu! \v 17 Utajiri mwingi kiasi hiki, nao umeharibiwa katika saa moja!"
sw.R: Wafanyabiashara waliotajirika kwa kumuuzia vitu hivyo watasimama mbali. Wataogopa mateso yake. Watalia na kuhuzunika. \v 16 Watasema, "Ni msiba mkubwa! Msiba mkubwa umeupata mji mkuu! Ulivaa kitani safi na nguo za zambarau na nyekundu. Ulivaa dhahabu, vito na lulu. \v 17 Katika saa moja tu utajiri wake wote umetoweka!"

es.L: Los comerciantes de estas cosas, los que se enriquecieron por ella, se pararán a lo lejos por el temor de su tormento, llorando y haciendo duelo, \v 16 diciendo: «¡Ay, ay, la gran ciudad, la que estaba vestida de lino fino y de púrpura y de escarlata, y adornada de oro y de piedras preciosas y de perlas, \v 17 porque en una hora ha sido arrasada tanta riqueza!».
es.B: Los que comerciaban con estas cosas y se habían enriquecido gracias a ella se mantendrán a distancia por miedo a su tormento, llorando y haciendo duelo: \v 16 «¡Ay, ay de la gran ciudad, que se vestía de lino fino, púrpura y escarlata, y se adornaba con oro, piedras preciosas y perlas! \v 17 ¡Tanta riqueza, y en una sola hora ha quedado arruinada!».
es.R: Los comerciantes que se hicieron ricos vendiéndole estas cosas se quedarán lejos. Tendrán miedo de su sufrimiento. Llorarán y estarán tristes. \v 16 Dirán: «¡Qué terrible! ¡Qué terrible para la gran ciudad! Se vestía de lino fino y de ropa de color púrpura y rojo. Llevaba oro, joyas y perlas. \v 17 ¡En solo una hora todas sus riquezas han desaparecido!».

decisions.choice: the laments over Tyre in Ezekiel 26-27
decisions.reason: The laments of kings, merchants and sailors follow Ezekiel's laments over Tyre, the great trading city, whose fall the princes of the coast, the merchants and the seamen mourned from a distance (Ezekiel 26:15-18; 27:28-36). Babylon's mourners grieve for their own losses more than for her.

decisions.choice: her clothing: the prostitute of 17:4
decisions.reason: The city is described in the words used of the woman in 17:4: the city and the prostitute are one.

source.text: Καὶ πᾶς κυβερνήτης καὶ πᾶς ὁ ἐπὶ τόπον πλέων, καὶ ναῦται καὶ ὅσοι τὴν θάλασσαν ἐργάζονται, ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἔστησαν καὶ ἔκραξαν βλέποντες τὸν καπνὸν τῆς πυρώσεως αὐτῆς λέγοντες· Τίς ὁμοία τῇ πόλει τῇ μεγάλῃ;

records.literal_gloss: And every helmsman and every one the to a place sailing and sailors and as many as the sea work, from afar stood \v 18 and cried out seeing the smoke of the burning of her, saying: What like to the city the great?

en.L: And every ship's captain and everyone who sails to any place, and sailors, and all who work the sea, stood far off \v 18 and cried out as they saw the smoke of her burning, saying, "What [city] is like the great city?"
en.B: Every helmsman, every traveler by sea, the sailors and all who work on the sea kept their distance \v 18 and shouted as they looked at the smoke of her burning: "What city was like the great city?"
en.R: Every ship captain, every passenger, every sailor, and everyone who earns a living on the sea stood far away. \v 18 They saw the smoke from her burning and shouted, "There was never a city as great as this one!"

fr.L: Et tout pilote, et quiconque navigue vers quelque lieu, et les marins, et tous ceux qui travaillent sur la mer, se tinrent au loin \v 18 et crièrent en voyant la fumée de son incendie, disant : « Quelle [ville est] semblable à la grande ville ? »
fr.B: Tous les pilotes, tous ceux qui voyagent par mer, les marins et tous ceux qui travaillent sur la mer se tinrent à distance \v 18 et s’écrièrent en regardant la fumée de son incendie : « Quelle ville était semblable à la grande ville ? »
fr.R: Tous les capitaines de navire, tous les passagers, tous les marins et tous ceux qui gagnent leur vie sur la mer sont restés loin. \v 18 Ils ont vu la fumée de son incendie et ils ont crié : « Il n’y a jamais eu de ville aussi grande que celle-ci ! »

sw.L: Na kila nahodha na kila asafiriye kwenda mahali [popote], na mabaharia na wote wanaofanya kazi baharini, walisimama mbali \v 18 na kupiga kelele walipouona moshi wa kuungua kwake, wakisema, "[Ni mji] gani ulio kama mji ule mkubwa?"
sw.B: Kila nahodha, kila msafiri wa baharini, mabaharia na wote wanaofanya kazi baharini walikaa mbali \v 18 na kupiga kelele walipoutazama moshi wa kuungua kwake: "Ni mji gani uliokuwa kama mji huu mkubwa?"
sw.R: Kila nahodha wa meli, kila abiria, kila baharia na kila mtu anayepata riziki yake baharini alisimama mbali. \v 18 Waliona moshi wa kuungua kwake, wakapiga kelele, "Hakujawahi kuwa na mji mkubwa kama huu!"

es.L: Y todo piloto, y todo el que navega a cualquier lugar, y los marineros, y todos los que trabajan en el mar, se pararon a lo lejos \v 18 y gritaban al ver el humo de su incendio, diciendo: «¿Qué [ciudad era] semejante a la gran ciudad?».
es.B: Todos los pilotos, todos los que viajaban por mar, los marineros y todos los que trabajan en el mar se mantuvieron a distancia \v 18 y gritaban al ver el humo de su incendio: «¿Qué ciudad hubo semejante a la gran ciudad?».
es.R: Todos los capitanes de barco, todos los pasajeros, todos los marineros y todos los que se ganan la vida en el mar se quedaron lejos. \v 18 Vieron el humo del incendio y gritaron: «¡Nunca hubo una ciudad tan grande como esta!».

decisions.choice: the seamen's lament: Ezekiel 27:28-32
decisions.reason: In Ezekiel the pilots and sailors stand on the shore, cry out bitterly, throw dust on their heads, and ask, "Who is like Tyre?" (Ezekiel 27:28-32). The question here echoes the world's praise of the beast (13:4).

decisions.choice: a statement (R)
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the rhetorical question.

decisions.choice: pilote (L, B); capitaine de navire (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is the man who steers the ship; French "pilote" has that sense and is the usual word in older and newer translations alike. "Timonier" is too technical. Readable says "capitaine", as the English does, the word a young reader knows.

decisions.choice: piloto (L, B); capitán de barco (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is the man who steered and commanded the ship; "piloto" is the Spanish word for that office, and Readable says "capitán".

source.text: καὶ ἔβαλον χοῦν ἐπὶ τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτῶν καὶ ἔκραξαν κλαίοντες καὶ πενθοῦντες λέγοντες· Οὐαὶ οὐαί, ἡ πόλις ἡ μεγάλη, ἐν ᾗ ἐπλούτησαν πάντες οἱ ἔχοντες τὰ πλοῖα ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ ἐκ τῆς τιμιότητος αὐτῆς, ὅτι μιᾷ ὥρᾳ ἠρημώθη.

records.literal_gloss: And they threw dust on the heads of them and cried out weeping and mourning, saying: Woe woe, the city the great, in which became rich all those having the ships in the sea from the wealth of her, because in one hour she was laid waste.

en.L: And they threw dust on their heads and cried out, weeping and mourning, saying, "Woe, woe, the great city, in which all who had ships on the sea grew rich from her wealth, for in one hour she has been laid waste!"
en.B: Throwing dust on their heads, weeping and mourning, they cried: "Woe, woe for the great city! Her wealth made rich everyone who owned a ship at sea, and in one hour she has been laid waste."
en.R: They threw dust on their heads to show their sorrow. They cried and shouted, "How terrible! How terrible for the great city! Everyone who owned ships became rich because of her riches. But in just one hour she has been destroyed!"

fr.L: Et ils jetèrent de la poussière sur leurs têtes, et ils crièrent, pleurant et en deuil, disant : « Malheur, malheur, ô grande ville, dans laquelle se sont enrichis par son opulence tous ceux qui avaient des navires sur la mer, car en une heure elle a été dévastée ! »
fr.B: Jetant de la poussière sur leur tête, pleurant et se lamentant, ils s’écrièrent : « Malheur, malheur à la grande ville ! Son opulence a enrichi tous ceux qui avaient un navire sur la mer, et en une heure elle a été dévastée. »
fr.R: Ils ont jeté de la poussière sur leur tête pour montrer leur tristesse. Ils ont pleuré et crié : « Quel malheur ! Quel malheur pour la grande ville ! Tous ceux qui avaient des bateaux sont devenus riches grâce à ses richesses. Mais en une heure seulement, elle a été détruite ! »

sw.L: Nao wakatupa mavumbi juu ya vichwa vyao na kupiga kelele, wakilia na kuomboleza, wakisema, "Ole, ole, mji ule mkubwa, ambamo wote wenye meli baharini walitajirika kutokana na utajiri wake, kwa sababu katika saa moja umefanywa ukiwa!"
sw.B: Wakitupa mavumbi juu ya vichwa vyao, wakilia na kuomboleza, walipiga kelele: "Ole, ole, mji mkuu! Utajiri wake uliwatajirisha wote waliokuwa na meli baharini, na katika saa moja umefanywa ukiwa."
sw.R: Walitupa mavumbi juu ya vichwa vyao kuonyesha huzuni yao. Walilia na kupiga kelele, "Ni msiba mkubwa! Msiba mkubwa umeupata mji mkuu! Kila mtu mwenye meli alitajirika kwa sababu ya utajiri wake. Lakini katika saa moja tu umeharibiwa kabisa!"

es.L: Y echaron polvo sobre sus cabezas, y gritaban, llorando y haciendo duelo, diciendo: «¡Ay, ay, la gran ciudad, en la cual se enriquecieron todos los que tenían naves en el mar por su opulencia, porque en una hora ha sido arrasada!».
es.B: Se echaron polvo sobre la cabeza, y llorando y haciendo duelo gritaban: «¡Ay, ay de la gran ciudad! Con su riqueza se enriquecieron todos los que tenían barcos en el mar, ¡y en una sola hora ha quedado arrasada!».
es.R: Se echaron polvo sobre la cabeza para mostrar su tristeza. Lloraban y gritaban: «¡Qué terrible! ¡Qué terrible para la gran ciudad! Todos los dueños de barcos se hicieron ricos con sus riquezas. ¡Pero en solo una hora ha sido destruida!».

decisions.choice: dust on the head: a sign of mourning
decisions.reason: Throwing dust on one's head was a sign of grief and humiliation (Joshua 7:6; Ezekiel 27:30).

source.text: Εὐφραίνου ἐπ’ αὐτῇ, οὐρανέ, καὶ οἱ ἅγιοι καὶ οἱ ἀπόστολοι καὶ οἱ προφῆται, ὅτι ἔκρινεν ὁ θεὸς τὸ κρίμα ὑμῶν ἐξ αὐτῆς.

records.literal_gloss: Rejoice over her, heaven, and the saints and the apostles and the prophets, because judged the God the judgment of you out of her.

en.L: Rejoice over her, heaven, and [you] saints and apostles and prophets, for God has judged your case against her!
en.B: Celebrate her fall, heaven, and you holy people, apostles, and prophets! God has taken up your case against her and judged it.
en.R: Heaven, be happy because of what happened to her! God's people, apostles, and prophets, be happy! God has punished her for what she did to you.

fr.L: Réjouis-toi à son sujet, ciel, et [vous,] les saints et les apôtres et les prophètes, car Dieu a jugé votre cause contre elle !
fr.B: Réjouis-toi de sa chute, ciel, et vous, le peuple saint de Dieu, les apôtres et les prophètes ! Dieu a pris votre cause en main contre elle et l’a jugée.
fr.R: Ciel, réjouis-toi de ce qui lui est arrivé ! Peuple de Dieu, apôtres et prophètes, réjouissez-vous ! Dieu l’a punie pour ce qu’elle vous a fait.

sw.L: Furahi juu yake, ewe mbingu, na [ninyi] watakatifu na mitume na manabii, kwa sababu Mungu ameihukumu hukumu yenu dhidi yake!
sw.B: Furahini kwa kuanguka kwake, enyi mbingu, nanyi watu watakatifu wa Mungu, mitume na manabii! Mungu ameishughulikia kesi yenu dhidi yake na kumhukumu.
sw.R: Mbingu, furahini kwa sababu ya yaliyompata! Watu wa Mungu, mitume na manabii, furahini! Mungu amemwadhibu kwa yale aliyowatendea ninyi.

es.L: ¡Alégrate sobre ella, cielo, y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, los santos y los apóstoles y los profetas, porque Dios ha juzgado {{plural_you:la causa de ustedes|vuestra causa}} contra ella!
es.B: ¡Celebra su caída, cielo, y {{plural_you:celebren|celebrad}} {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, pueblo santo de Dios, apóstoles y profetas! Dios ha tomado {{plural_you:la causa de ustedes|vuestra causa}} contra ella y la ha juzgado.
es.R: ¡Cielo, alégrate por lo que le ha pasado! ¡Pueblo de Dios, apóstoles y profetas, {{plural_you:alégrense|alegraos}}! Dios la ha castigado por lo que ella {{plural_you:les|os}} hizo.

decisions.choice: God has judged your case against her
alternatives: God has turned on her the judgment she passed on you
decisions.reason: "Judged your judgment from her" is an unusual phrase. It most likely means that God has given judgment in favor of his people against the city that condemned them, answering the martyrs' cry for justice (6:10; 19:2). It may also mean that the sentence she passed on them now falls on her.

decisions.choice: joy at God's justice, not at suffering
decisions.reason: Heaven rejoices that God has vindicated his people and ended the city's oppression (19:1-3). The call contrasts with the self-pity of those who shared her sins (18:9-19).

decisions.choice: saints (L); holy people (B); God's people (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:8.

decisions.choice: les saints (L); le peuple saint de Dieu (B); le peuple de Dieu (R), here and in 18:24
decisions.reason: As in 17:6 and the style guide's term for the whole New Testament.

decisions.choice: alégrate (cielo, singular) ... {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} (the saints, plural)
decisions.reason: The Greek command is singular, to heaven; the saints, apostles and prophets are then named, and the "your" that follows is plural, so Spanish keeps the singular for heaven and uses plural_you for the rest.

source.text: Καὶ ἦρεν εἷς ἄγγελος ἰσχυρὸς λίθον ὡς μύλινον μέγαν, καὶ ἔβαλεν εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν λέγων· Οὕτως ὁρμήματι βληθήσεται Βαβυλὼν ἡ μεγάλη πόλις, καὶ οὐ μὴ εὑρεθῇ ἔτι.

records.literal_gloss: And took up one angel mighty a stone like a millstone great and threw into the sea, saying: Thus with violence will be thrown Babylon the great city, and not not will be found any longer.

en.L: And a mighty angel took up a stone like a great millstone and threw [it] into the sea, saying, "Thus with violence Babylon the great city will be thrown down, and will never be found again.
en.B: A strong angel picked up a stone like a huge millstone and flung it into the sea. "Like this," he said, "violently, Babylon the great city will be hurled down, and no one will find her any more.
en.R: Then a powerful angel picked up a large stone, as big as a millstone for grinding grain. He threw it into the sea and said, "That is how the great city of Babylon will be thrown down. No one will ever see it again.

fr.L: Et un ange puissant souleva une pierre semblable à une grande meule et [la] jeta dans la mer, disant : « Ainsi, avec violence, sera précipitée Babylone, la grande ville, et on ne la trouvera plus jamais.
fr.B: Un ange vigoureux prit une pierre semblable à une énorme meule et la lança dans la mer. « C’est ainsi, dit-il, avec violence, que Babylone, la grande ville, sera précipitée, et on ne la retrouvera plus jamais.
fr.R: Puis un ange puissant a soulevé une grosse pierre, aussi grosse qu’une meule pour moudre le grain. Il l’a jetée dans la mer et il a dit : « C’est comme ça que Babylone, la grande ville, sera renversée. Plus personne ne la verra jamais.

sw.L: Na malaika mmoja mwenye nguvu akainua jiwe kama jiwe kubwa la kusagia, akalitupa baharini, akisema, "Hivyo kwa nguvu Babeli, mji ule mkubwa, utatupwa chini, wala hautaonekana tena kamwe.
sw.B: Malaika mmoja mwenye nguvu aliokota jiwe kama jiwe kubwa la kusagia, akalitupa baharini, akasema: "Hivi ndivyo, kwa nguvu nyingi, Babeli, mji mkuu, utakavyotupwa chini, wala hakuna atakayeuona tena.
sw.R: Kisha malaika mwenye nguvu akainua jiwe kubwa, kubwa kama jiwe la kusagia nafaka. Alilitupa baharini, akasema, "Hivyo ndivyo Babeli, ule mji mkuu, utakavyotupwa chini. Hakuna mtu atakayeuona tena kamwe.

es.L: Y un ángel poderoso levantó una piedra como una gran piedra de molino y [la] arrojó al mar, diciendo: «Así, con violencia, será arrojada Babilonia la gran ciudad, y nunca más será hallada.
es.B: Un ángel poderoso levantó una piedra como una enorme piedra de molino y la lanzó al mar. «Así —dijo—, con esta violencia será derribada Babilonia, la gran ciudad, y nadie la volverá a encontrar.
es.R: Luego un ángel poderoso levantó una piedra grande, tan grande como una piedra de molino para moler grano. La arrojó al mar y dijo: «Así será derribada la gran ciudad de Babilonia. Nadie la volverá a ver jamás.

decisions.choice: a stone thrown into the sea: Jeremiah 51:63-64
decisions.reason: Jeremiah told Seraiah to tie a stone to the scroll of Babylon's doom and throw it into the Euphrates, saying, "Thus shall Babylon sink, to rise no more" (Jeremiah 51:63-64). A millstone was a large, heavy stone, sometimes turned by a donkey (compare Mark 9:42).

decisions.choice: the angel's words run to 18:24
decisions.reason: The angel speaks to the end of the chapter, addressing the city as "you" in 18:22-23.

source.text: καὶ φωνὴ κιθαρῳδῶν καὶ μουσικῶν καὶ αὐλητῶν καὶ σαλπιστῶν οὐ μὴ ἀκουσθῇ ἐν σοὶ ἔτι, καὶ πᾶς τεχνίτης πάσης τέχνης οὐ μὴ εὑρεθῇ ἐν σοὶ ἔτι, καὶ φωνὴ μύλου οὐ μὴ ἀκουσθῇ ἐν σοὶ ἔτι, καὶ φῶς λύχνου οὐ μὴ φάνῃ ἐν σοὶ ἔτι, καὶ φωνὴ νυμφίου καὶ νύμφης οὐ μὴ ἀκουσθῇ ἐν σοὶ ἔτι· ὅτι οἱ ἔμποροί σου ἦσαν οἱ μεγιστᾶνες τῆς γῆς, ὅτι ἐν τῇ φαρμακείᾳ σου ἐπλανήθησαν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, καὶ ἐν αὐτῇ αἷμα προφητῶν καὶ ἁγίων εὑρέθη καὶ πάντων τῶν ἐσφαγμένων ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.

records.literal_gloss: And sound of harpists and musicians and flute players and trumpeters not not will be heard in you any longer, and every craftsman of every craft not not will be found in you any longer, and sound of millstone not not will be heard in you any longer, \v 23 and light of lamp not not will shine in you any longer, and voice of bridegroom and bride not not will be heard in you any longer; because the merchants of you were the great ones of the earth, because by the sorcery of you were deceived all the nations, \v 24 and in her blood of prophets and of saints was found and of all those having been slaughtered on the earth.

en.L: And the sound of harpists and musicians and flute players and trumpeters will never be heard in you again, and no craftsman of any craft will ever be found in you again, and the sound of a millstone will never be heard in you again, \v 23 and the light of a lamp will never shine in you again, and the voice of bridegroom and bride will never be heard in you again; for your merchants were the great ones of the earth, for by your sorcery all the nations were deceived, \v 24 and in her was found the blood of prophets and of saints and of all who have been slaughtered on the earth."
en.B: No more will the music of harpists and singers, of flute players and trumpeters, be heard in you; no craftsman of any trade will be found in you again; the sound of the millstone will be heard in you no more; \v 23 the light of a lamp will shine in you no more; the voices of bridegroom and bride will be heard in you no more. For your merchants were the great ones of the earth, and by your sorcery all the nations were led astray. \v 24 The blood of prophets and of God's holy people was found in her, the blood of all who have been slaughtered on the earth."
en.R: No one will ever play music in you again, on harps, flutes, or trumpets. No one will ever work at any trade in you again. No one will ever grind grain in you again. \v 23 No lamp will ever shine in you again. No one will ever celebrate a wedding in you again. Your merchants were the most important people in the world, and you fooled all the nations with your magic. \v 24 The blood of the prophets and of God's people was found in that city, and the blood of everyone who was killed on the earth."

fr.L: Et le son des joueurs de harpe et des musiciens et des joueurs de flûte et des trompettistes ne sera plus jamais entendu en toi, et aucun artisan d’aucun métier ne sera plus jamais trouvé en toi, et le bruit de la meule ne sera plus jamais entendu en toi, \v 23 et la lumière d’une lampe ne brillera plus jamais en toi, et la voix de l’époux et de l’épouse ne sera plus jamais entendue en toi ; car tes marchands étaient les grands de la terre, car par ta sorcellerie toutes les nations ont été égarées, \v 24 et en elle a été trouvé le sang des prophètes et des saints, et de tous ceux qui ont été égorgés sur la terre. »
fr.B: Le son des joueurs de harpe et des chanteurs, des joueurs de flûte et des trompettistes, on ne l’entendra plus jamais en toi ; aucun artisan d’aucun métier ne se trouvera plus en toi ; le bruit de la meule, on ne l’entendra plus en toi ; \v 23 la lumière de la lampe ne brillera plus en toi ; la voix de l’époux et de l’épouse, on ne l’entendra plus en toi. fr.R: Plus personne ne jouera jamais de musique chez toi, ni sur la harpe, ni sur la flûte, ni à la trompette. Plus personne ne travaillera jamais chez toi à aucun métier. Tes marchands étaient les gens les plus importants du monde, et tu as trompé toutes les nations avec ta magie. \v 24 On a trouvé dans cette ville le sang des prophètes et du peuple de Dieu, et le sang de tous ceux qui ont été tués sur la terre. »

sw.L: Na sauti ya wapiga vinubi na wanamuziki na wapiga filimbi na wapiga tarumbeta haitasikika ndani yako tena kamwe, na fundi yeyote wa ufundi wowote hataonekana ndani yako tena kamwe, na sauti ya jiwe la kusagia haitasikika ndani yako tena kamwe, \v 23 na nuru ya taa haitaangaza ndani yako tena kamwe, na sauti ya bwana arusi na bibi arusi haitasikika ndani yako tena kamwe; kwa sababu wafanyabiashara wako walikuwa wakuu wa dunia, kwa sababu kwa uchawi wako mataifa yote yalidanganywa, \v 24 na ndani yake ilionekana damu ya manabii na ya watakatifu na ya wote waliochinjwa juu ya dunia."
sw.B: Muziki wa wapiga vinubi na waimbaji, wa wapiga filimbi na wapiga tarumbeta, hautasikika ndani yako tena kamwe; fundi wa kazi yoyote hataonekana ndani yako tena; sauti ya jiwe la kusagia haitasikika ndani yako tena; \v 23 nuru ya taa haitaangaza ndani yako tena; sauti za bwana arusi na bibi arusi hazitasikika ndani yako tena. Kwa maana wafanyabiashara wako walikuwa wakuu wa dunia, na kwa uchawi wako mataifa yote yalipotoshwa. \v 24 Damu ya manabii na ya watu watakatifu wa Mungu ilionekana ndani yake, damu ya wote waliochinjwa duniani."
sw.R: Hakuna mtu atakayepiga tena muziki ndani yako, kwa vinubi, filimbi au tarumbeta. Hakuna mtu atakayefanya tena kazi ya ufundi wowote ndani yako. Hakuna mtu atakayesaga tena nafaka ndani yako. \v 23 Hakuna taa itakayoangaza tena ndani yako. Hakuna mtu atakayesherehekea tena arusi ndani yako. Wafanyabiashara wako walikuwa watu muhimu kuliko wote duniani, nawe uliyadanganya mataifa yote kwa uchawi wako. \v 24 Damu ya manabii na ya watu wa Mungu ilionekana katika mji huo, na damu ya kila mtu aliyeuawa duniani."

es.L: Y el sonido de arpistas y de músicos y de flautistas y de trompetistas nunca más se oirá en ti, y ningún artesano de ningún oficio será hallado más en ti, y el sonido del molino nunca más se oirá en ti, \v 23 y la luz de la lámpara nunca más brillará en ti, y la voz del novio y de la novia nunca más se oirá en ti; porque tus comerciantes eran los grandes de la tierra, porque por tu hechicería fueron engañadas todas las naciones, \v 24 y en ella se halló la sangre de profetas y de santos y de todos los que han sido degollados sobre la tierra».
es.B: Nunca más se oirá en ti la música de arpistas y cantores, de flautistas y trompetistas; nunca más se hallará en ti artesano de ningún oficio; nunca más se oirá en ti el ruido del molino; \v 23 nunca más brillará en ti la luz de una lámpara; nunca más se oirá en ti la voz del novio y de la novia. Porque tus comerciantes eran los grandes de la tierra, y con tu hechicería engañaste a todas las naciones. \v 24 En ella se halló la sangre de los profetas y del pueblo santo de Dios, la sangre de todos los que han sido degollados en la tierra».
es.R: Nunca más se tocará música en ti, ni con arpas, ni con flautas, ni con trompetas. Nunca más nadie trabajará en ti en ningún oficio. Nunca más se molerá grano en ti. \v 23 Nunca más brillará en ti una lámpara. Nunca más se celebrará una boda en ti. Tus comerciantes eran la gente más importante del mundo, y con tu magia engañaste a todas las naciones. \v 24 En esa ciudad se halló la sangre de los profetas y del pueblo de Dios, y la sangre de todos los que fueron asesinados en la tierra».

decisions.choice: the silence of a dead city: Jeremiah 25:10
decisions.reason: "I will banish from them the voice of mirth and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the sound of the millstones and the light of the lamp" (Jeremiah 25:10; compare 7:34; 16:9). Every sign of ordinary life, work, music and marriage, is gone.

decisions.choice: merchants who were princes: Tyre
decisions.reason: Isaiah 23:8 says of Tyre that "her merchants were princes". The city's wealth made traders into the world's great ones.

decisions.choice: sorcery: deception that bewitched the nations
decisions.reason: φαρμακείᾳ is magic or sorcery (9:21). Here it describes the city's seductive power, by which it led the nations astray.

decisions.choice: the blood of all who were slaughtered on the earth
decisions.reason: The city is held responsible for the blood of the prophets and saints, and of all who have been killed on the earth, as Jesus said of Jerusalem's leaders (Matthew 23:35). The city stands for the whole order of the world that sheds innocent blood. The address turns from "you" to "her" in this last sentence.

decisions.choice: saints (L); God's holy people (B); God's people (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:8.

decisions.choice: uchawi
decisions.reason: "Uchawi" (sorcery, magic), as settled for the Swahili New Testament; here it is the spell by which the city deceived the nations (m3).

decisions.choice: hechicería (L, B); magia (R)
decisions.reason: As in 9:21, where the related word is "hechicerías" and Readable says "practicar la magia".

decisions.choice: degollados
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of the Lamb "como degollado" in 5:6 and of the martyrs in 6:9; Literal and Balanced keep the same word so the link is heard.
